reason: The cited evidence does not directly address Y2O3 dispersion in MoNbTaW HEAs or its specific effects on mechanical and irradiation properties. E1 discusses precipitation strengthening in a different HEA system, E2 examines irradiation response of a Cr-V-containing HEA without oxides, and E3 only generally mentions that oxides can strengthen HEAs and pin grain boundaries, without providing specific data on Y2O3 in MoNbTaW. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Y2O3 nanoparticles can be uniformly dispersed in a MoNbTaW HEA via mechanical alloying and hot consolidation
Y2O3 nanoparticles act as obstacles to dislocation motion, enhancing precipitation strengthening
Y2O3 nanoparticles serve as efficient sinks for irradiation-induced point defects, suppressing defect coalescence
The ODS microstructure will remain stable under high temperature (~1200°C) and irradiation
The ODS alloy will exhibit higher yield strength and improved toughness compared to the baseline
